bio.en: Dmitry Zlokazov is Global Head of Product at Revolut, the $60B+ finance super app, known for hiring and incubating some of the best product managers in the industry.
bio.zh: Dmitry Zlokazov 是 Revolut 的全球产品负责人，Revolut 是一家估值超 600 亿美元的金融超级应用，以招聘和培养业内最优秀的产品经理而闻名。

summary.en: Dmitry explains Revolut's product philosophy: valuing raw intellect and unquenched hunger over experience, and never compromising on quality, UX, and aesthetics even when cutting features. He argues if a product is 99% done it's closer to 0% than 100%, and shares how the company produces and hires great product leaders. The conversation centers on ownership, solving painful problems, and making experiences “wow and lovable.”
summary.zh: Dmitry 解释了 Revolut 的产品哲学：看重原始智力和不屈的饥饿感甚于经验，即便砍功能也绝不妥协质量、UX 与美感。他认为若产品“完成 99%”反而更接近 0% 而非 100%，并分享了公司如何培养与招聘优秀产品领导者。对话聚焦拥有感、解决痛点，以及打造“惊艳且讨人喜欢”的体验。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Everyone is striving for talented, skillful, smart people. Revolut values way more raw intellect and this unquenched hunger to build things rather than experience.
turns.zh: 每个人都在努力寻找有才华、有技能、聪明的人。 Revolut 更看重的是原始智慧和对构建事物而不是经验的永不满足的渴望。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I hear one of the ways you approach early products differently is you guys invest a lot in actually making it good.
turns.zh: 我听说你们处理早期产品的不同方式之一是你们投入大量资金来真正使其变得更好。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: It's not getting traction. Is it because the underlying idea is wrong? Or maybe your product just sucks? By forcing everyone to build a product that people will love, we kind of cut out this part of uncertainty. We can cut down the product in terms of functionality to just most critical features, but we will never compromise on the quality and UX and the aesthetics.
turns.zh: 它没有得到牵引力。是因为底层的想法是错误的吗？或者也许你的产品很糟糕？通过强迫每个人打造人们会喜欢的产品，我们就消除了这部分不确定性。我们可以将产品的功能缩减为最关键的功能，但我们永远不会在质量、用户体验和美观上妥协。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything that you've figured out about just how to set up new products for success?
turns.zh: 关于如何开发新产品以取得成功，您有什么想法吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: If something is 99% done, it's closer to 0% rather than 100%.
turns.zh: 如果某件事完成了 99%，那么它更接近 0%，而不是 100%。

turns.en: As you know, I've been doing a bunch of research into which companies hire and create the best product managers, and I've been triangulating this across a bunch of different data points. turns.zh: 如您所知，我一直在对哪些公司雇用和培养最好的产品经理进行了大量研究，并且我一直在通过一系列不同的数据点对此进行三角测量。我一直在研究哪些公司的校友产品经理在离开公司时晋升最多，在离开公司时成为首席产品官的比例最高，在初创公司成为第一位 PM，也创办了自己的公司。当我对所有这些不同的数据点进行三角测量时，有 3 家公司位居榜首，即 Revolut、Palantir 和 Intercom。 (00:04:21)：显然你们正在做一些非常特别的事情。我认为没有很多人，特别是在美国，对 Revolut 了解很多，所以我很高兴您能来到这里。我真的很高兴能够从你们那里汲取尽可能多的智慧，了解你们在帮助招聘和培训产品经理方面所取得的成果。所以我想首先让人们稍微了解一下 Revolut 是什么。我认为很多人尤其是美国人对此不太了解。那么了解你们所做的事情的最简单方法是什么？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Revolut challenges banks in 50 different countries and it all started 10 years ago in London. So maybe let me give you a bit of a context, especially for someone based in the US, it's important to understand that European banking landscape is very diverse. In the US if you travel from state to state, things are different, but for example, you always pay in US dollars, right? In the UK you pay in British Pound. If you travel to mainland Europe, you will pay in Euro, but if you go to Switzerland, you'll pay in Swiss francs. If you go to Sweden, you'll pay in Swedish Krona and so on and so-and-so. Overall, there are 25 different currencies and every time you were traveling and paying in a different currency, banks were charging you exorbitant fees on top of terrible foreign exchange rates, and that's when Revolut launched as a multi-currency card and people loved it. (00:05:51): They loved that Revolut was saving them 50 or 100 euros, but even more so they loved the transparency and simplicity of the product and that's why when we started rolling out more and more products based on those principles, they were quickly getting trust of people. They were quickly getting traction. So that's how P2P transfers appeared, and then frictionless crypto buying and withdrawal to a bank account appeared. And then more and more products created products, savings products and so on.
turns.zh: Revolut 向 50 个不同国家的银行发起挑战，这一切始于 10 年前的伦敦。因此，也许让我给您提供一些背景信息，尤其是对于美国的人来说，了解欧洲银行业格局非常多样化非常重要。在美国，如果您从一个州旅行到另一个州，情况会有所不同，但例如，您总是用美元付款，对吧？在英国，您用英镑支付。如果您前往欧洲大陆，您将用欧元支付，但如果您前往瑞士，您将用瑞士法郎支付。如果你去瑞典，你会用瑞典克朗等支付。总体而言，有 25 种不同的货币，每次您旅行并使用不同的货币付款时，银行除了糟糕的外汇汇率外还要向您收取高昂的费用，就在那时，Revolut 作为多币种卡推出，受到了人们的喜爱。 (00:05:51)：他们喜欢 Revolut 为他们节省了 50 或 100 欧元，但他们更喜欢产品的透明度和简单性，这就是为什么当我们开始推出越来越多基于这些原则的产品时，他们很快就赢得了人们的信任。他们很快就获得了关注。这就是 P2P 转账的出现方式，然后出现了无摩擦的加密货币购买和提取到银行账户的方式。然后越来越多的产品创造了产品、储蓄产品等等。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. And then just to give people a few kind of scale of the company, how many employees are there roughly? I think the last valuation something around 60 billion. I don't know if you can even comment on that, but just what are some numbers real quick for people to understand the scale of the company at this point?
turns.zh: 惊人的。然后给大家介绍一下公司的规模，大概有多少员工？我认为最后的估值大约在 600 亿左右。我不知道你是否可以对此发表评论，但目前有哪些数字可以让人们真正快速了解公司的规模？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: The headcount is not something we're trying to increase, to be honest. Actually Revolut tries to stay as lean as possible, but I think it's just that our appetite for growth is so big that I think we're currently at maybe 6 or 7,000 employees.
turns.zh: 老实说，我们并不想增加员工人数。事实上，Revolut 试图尽可能保持精简，但我认为这只是我们对增长的渴望太大了，我认为我们目前可能有 6 或 7,000 名员工。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. Okay, cool. So let's get into what you've learned about building an amazing product team and also hiring an amazing product team. So first of all, you call your product managers product owners, and when we were chatting through initially it was like, "Oh, I see. It's just like a big scrum business," and they just have all these product owners who many times on this podcast people have talked about that's not actually a product manager, but that's not at all how you work. So in this context, product owner's an actual owner. Talk about just the story behind why you call your product managers, product owners.
turns.zh: 哇。好吧，酷。因此，让我们来了解一下您在建立一支出色的产品团队以及雇用一支出色的产品团队方面所学到的知识。所以首先，你把你的产品经理称为产品负责人，当我们最初聊天时，就像是，“哦，我明白了。这就像一个大的 Scrum 业务，”他们只是拥有所有这些产品负责人，人们在这个播客上多次谈到，这实际上并不是产品经理，但这根本不是你的工作方式。因此，在这种情况下，产品所有者是实际所有者。只谈谈为什么你打电话给你的产品经理、产品负责人背后的故事。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, it's not a scrum term for us, it's just our take on emphasizing how ownership is important, really. So product owners are central to the company and its growth. They are end-to-end responsible for the product, for this part of the business, and for their customers to be happy. And for that, they do really everything. They run the teams, they define which roadmap we need to build to improve certain business metrics, and they also contribute to high-level company strategy, but then most importantly, they execute on it relentlessly and they are ultimate responsible for the product to be shipped and achieve results.
turns.zh: 是的，这对我们来说不是一个 Scrum 术语，这只是我们强调所有权的重要性，真的。因此，产品负责人对于公司及其发展至关重要。他们对产品、这部分业务以及让客户满意负有端到端的责任。为此，他们竭尽全力。他们管理团队，定义我们需要构建哪些路线图来改进某些业务指标，他们还为公司的高层战略做出贡献，但最重要的是，他们坚持不懈地执行该战略，并对要交付的产品和实现结果负有最终责任。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's always this term of mini-CEO, PM as a mini-CEO, and it feels like in your context, that's actually what you try to do with your product team is they're essentially mini-CEOs. They have a lot of power. I think engineers, designers report to them. Is that right?
turns.zh: 总是有“迷你首席执行官”这个术语，PM 作为迷你首席执行官，感觉就像在你的环境中，这实际上是你试图对你的产品团队做的事情，他们本质上是迷你首席执行官。他们有很大的权力。我认为工程师、设计师向他们汇报。是这样吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, correct. Well, I prefer to say local CEO.
turns.zh: 是的，正确。嗯，我更喜欢说本地CEO。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Local CEO. Okay, let's talk about that. Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: 当地首席执行官。好吧，我们来谈谈这个吧。是啊是啊。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, but that's true. So the way we operate, we have these fully cross-functional teams, meaning they're staffed with all necessary functions, engineers data, analysts, designers, operational managers and so on. And we also operate in metrics. So everyone has a line manager and a functional manager. So product owner is always the line manager for everyone on the team, meaning product owner defines what they need to do, but then functional managers, they define how these things are need to be built and essentially with the right level of quality and so on.
turns.zh: 是的，但那是真的。因此，我们的运作方式是，我们拥有这些完全跨职能的团队，这意味着他们配备了所有必要的职能、工程师数据、分析师、设计师、运营经理等。我们也按照指标进行操作。所以每个人都有一个直线经理和一个职能经理。因此，产品负责人始终是团队中每个人的直线经理，这意味着产品负责人定义他们需要做什么，然后职能经理定义这些东西需要如何构建，并且本质上具有正确的质量水平等等。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this because it's so fun just to learn about such different ways of operating. Another fact that I saw is that there's two types of product owners. There's kind of like a UX product owner, and then there's a different like technical product owner.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个，因为了解如此不同的操作方式非常有趣。我看到的另一个事实是，有两种类型的产品所有者。有一种类似于用户体验产品所有者，然后有一种不同的类似技术产品所有者。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: We actually have three.
turns.zh: 我们实际上有三个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Three.
turns.zh: 三。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: And the third type becomes increasingly more important. So the first type is UX product owners. Then there are technical product owners, and then there are data science product owners. So UX product owners are the ones who work on consumer facing part of the product. Usually they have a great taste for things and they understand what constitutes UX that will work and which things will not work. So they also have this expertise in the industry. Then tech product owners, they are the ones who delve deepest into details. Usually those are former engineers who grew into making decisions and driving business. And the data science product owners are usually former data scientists who decided to grow into management positions, but they're still very hands-on. (00:10:55): And you know what? There are way more things that are common to each of these three specializations. So what we see sometimes is people just shifting them because I would say that what defines the specialization is probably 5, 10, 15% while 85 to 90% is common to each one of them. And those things are, so first of all, being a great problem solver and have a great linear thinking, but also have a creative approach towards nonlinear problems. Then building this context for customer and building empathy towards customer and translating it into the team. (00:11:48): Then going down to details very, very deep because in our domain there are no obvious things and you need to get to the root cause of the problem really, really deep to understand what will work and what will not work. And that means that you also need to be quite technical, even if you are an expert, you still need to often go as deep as sitting with engineers and reading code. And then I would also emphasize the importance of business acumen because we tend to measure and quantify product performance a lot. And you need to understand, okay, what things will we build that will drive eventually that business metric and that target?
turns.zh: 第三种类型变得越来越重要。所以第一类是UX产品所有者。然后是技术产品所有者，然后是数据科学产品所有者。因此，用户体验产品负责人是负责产品中面向消费者的部分的人。通常他们对事物有很好的品味，并且了解什么构成用户体验有效，哪些无效。所以他们也有这个行业的专业知识。然后是技术产品所有者，他们是最深入研究细节的人。通常这些人都是前工程师，后来成长为决策者和推动业务的人。数据科学产品负责人通常是前数据科学家，后来决定晋升为管理职位，但他们仍然非常亲力亲为。 (00:10:55)：你知道吗？这三个专业都有更多的共同点。所以我们有时会看到人们只是在改变它们，因为我想说，定义专业化的可能是 5%、10%、15%，而 85% 到 90% 对他们每个人来说都是共同的。首先，这些东西是一个出色的问题解决者，具有出色的线性思维，而且对非线性问题也有创造性的方法。然后为客户建立这种背景，建立对客户的同理心，并将其转化为团队。 (00:11:48)：然后非常非常深入地讨论细节，因为在我们的领域中没有明显的事情，你需要非常非常深入地找到问题的根本原因，以了解什么有效，什么无效。这意味着你还需要具备相当的技术水平，即使你是专家，你仍然需要经常深入地与工程师坐在一起阅读代码。然后我还要强调商业头脑的重要性，因为我们倾向于大量衡量和量化产品性能。您需要了解，好吧，我们将构建哪些东西来最终推动业务指标和目标？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So I love this idea of the product owners having to go really deep. I think a lot of people hearing this, they think they can go deep, go deep, really understand the details of what they're working on. I'm curious if there's an example that's illustrative of just what you actually mean here.
turns.zh: 所以我喜欢产品负责人必须深入研究的想法。我想很多人听到这个，他们认为他们可以深入，深入，真正理解他们正在做的事情的细节。我很好奇是否有一个例子可以说明您在这里的实际含义。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: For example, to provide the best possible product in every country of presence, we need to have necessary licenses. In Europe, it means that we need to launch local branches of our European bank, for example, a branch for France, a branch for Germany, or a branch for Italy. To launch a branch, you need to fully comply with all necessary regulation. You need to report necessary data on customers to various regulators and authorities. You need to register with local payment systems. And each of these things, they have a lot of projects nested within. We have a very lean team of just a few people who need to scope everything and do it at the scale of 50 countries. So the way we do it is we go very deep on example of each of these projects. For example, we launched a branch in Ireland, we launched a branch in Netherlands. (00:14:01): Then we reverse engineered what was the best process to do it, and then we went back up on top level and we said, okay, but what's the ideal framework of doing it at scale? And then we formalized it into a process really like an algorithmic process with steps and quality gates and assay needs, what people do we need to hire and how soon do we need to start doing that before we want to launch a new country. Then, so it's not only going deep, but also being flexible and doing this switch between zooming in very deep and then raising on the level of helicopter view and then understanding, okay, so this seems very, very complex in details, but then when you zoom out, how can we simplify it and build a robust process around it, which is scalable? And that's something that we have to do a lot.
turns.zh: 例如，为了在每个开展业务的国家/地区提供最好的产品，我们需要拥有必要的许可证。在欧洲，这意味着我们需要在欧洲银行设立当地分行，例如法国分行、德国分行或意大利分行。要开设分支机构，您需要完全遵守所有必要的法规。您需要向各个监管机构和当局报告有关客户的必要数据。您需要在当地支付系统注册。每一个东西都嵌套了很多项目。我们有一个非常精干的团队，只有几个人，他们需要确定一切范围并在 50 个国家/地区的范围内开展工作。因此，我们的做法是深入研究每个项目的示例。例如，我们在爱尔兰设立了分支机构，在荷兰设立了分支机构。 (00:14:01)：然后我们对最佳流程进行了逆向工程，然后我们回到顶层，我们说，好吧，但是大规模实现这一目标的理想框架是什么？然后我们将其正式化为一个非常类似于算法流程的流程，其中包含步骤、质量门控和分析需求，我们需要雇用哪些人员，以及在我们想要启动一个新国家之前我们需要多长时间开始这样做。然后，它不仅要深入，而且要灵活，在放大到非常深的深度和提升直升机视图的水平之间进行切换，然后理解，好吧，所以这在细节上看起来非常非常复杂，但是当你缩小时，我们如何简化它并围绕它构建一个健壮的流程，这是可扩展的？这是我们必须做的很多事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: As you're talking and we go through this chat, I'm keeping kind of track of what I think is most contributing to your alumni product owners, product managers becoming so successful. So a couple of things so far that I think are probably contributing to this is one is just having a lot of ownership over what they're building, which leads to building skills to start companies and become leaders at other companies. So these product owners that you have are just own a lot and are essentially GMs of whatever product they're working on. And then there's this depth and complexity where you have to really get good at understanding a problem really deeply. I imagine many of these people go on to work on something like that later, somewhere else because they've spent all this time, or they just get really good at dealing with complex many layered problems. So is there anything else just kind of along those lines as I say that you think is important?
turns.zh: 当你说话和我们进行这次聊天时，我一直在跟踪我认为对你的校友产品所有者、产品经理取得如此成功最有贡献的因素。到目前为止，我认为可能促成这一点的几件事是，对他们正在构建的东西拥有很大的所有权，这会导致培养创办公司并成为其他公司领导者的技能。因此，您拥有的这些产品负责人只是拥有很多东西，并且本质上是他们正在开发的任何产品的总经理。然后，在深度和复杂性方面，你必须真正擅长真正深入地理解问题。我想这些人中的许多人会继续在其他地方从事类似的工作，因为他们已经花了这么多时间，或者他们只是非常擅长处理复杂的多层次问题。那么，像我所说的那样，还有什么你认为重要的事情吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I would probably add an obsession with building wow product.
turns.zh: 我可能会痴迷于打造令人惊叹的产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. W-O-W?
turns.zh: 哇。哇？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: W-O-W.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool.
turns.zh: 凉爽的。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I think in FinTech overall, this is probably the most neglected part usually, but it's also a part that we at Revolut, we pay enormous attention to. So it's not only when you do a trade in the app or when you send money, it's very important for it to be very fast and cheap process for you so that you don't pay a lot of fees. But we also pay a lot of attention to look and feel of the app and how smooth it is and how frictionless the process. Not only we invest in reducing clicks and optimizing finals, but we also want people to feel that we really cared about them. We also want people to feel that we love our customers and we applied extra effort for the product to look great and feel great. And I hear this a lot from our customers, like the app is something they really love and it helps them solve their problems. It's at least one of the ingredients of the company's success. (00:17:22): And I think people that work at Revolut, they built habit of paying attention to these small nuances, small details that make the product lovable. And then second is handling this context because it's a lot of details where you need to dive, but there are also a lot of dimensions where you need to dive into different details. And I think this ability to keep this large context in your mind and consider second order effects and view subjects from multiple angles, I think that this is also a very important skill that people usually train at Revolut.
turns.zh: 我认为在金融科技整体上，这可能是通常最被忽视的部分，但它也是我们 Revolut 非常关注的部分。因此，不仅当您在应用程序中进行交易或汇款时，对您而言快速且便宜的流程非常重要，这样您就不必支付大量费用。但我们也非常关注应用程序的外观和感觉，以及它的流畅程度和过程的顺畅程度。我们不仅在减少点击量和优化决赛方面进行投资，而且还希望人们感到我们真正关心他们。我们还希望人们感受到我们爱我们的客户，并且我们付出了额外的努力让产品看起来很棒并且感觉很棒。我从我们的客户那里听到很多这样的说法，就像这个应用程序是他们真正喜欢的东西，它可以帮助他们解决问题。这至少是该公司成功的要素之一。 (00:17:22)：我认为在 Revolut 工作的人们养成了关注这些细微差别和小细节的习惯，正是这些细微差别和小细节使产品变得可爱。其次是处理这个上下文，因为你需要深入研究很多细节，但也有很多维度你需要深入研究不同的细节。我认为这种在头脑中记住这个大背景并考虑二阶效应并从多个角度看待主题的能力，我认为这也是人们通常在 Revolut 训练的一项非常重要的技能。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, cool. So we have three bullet points on the ingredients of great product managers slash owners that you guys incubate. On this wow piece, which I love. How do you operationalize this sort of thing? I imagine a big part of it is hiring people that are really good at this and value building lovable products. Is there any way you kind of have a process around making sure the things you ship are wow and lovable?
turns.zh: 好吧，酷。因此，我们对你们培养的优秀产品经理削减所有者的要素有三个要点。关于我喜欢的这件令人惊叹的作品。您如何实施此类事情？我想其中很大一部分是雇用真正擅长于此并重视打造可爱产品的人。有没有什么办法可以确保你发布的东西令人惊叹且可爱？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Two things that you need to understand about how Revolut operates is that we operate in small lean teams that are tasked to build products and as I mentioned, and having end-to-end responsibility for products. And usually they're the ones who build it from zero and then they're growing and developing this product. And then another thing is that company is very flat and hierarchy is very flat. We still have our founders, Nick and Vlad, very hands-on going down to details for every product and every part of the business. And every week they have product reviews with every team giving an opportunity to every product owner present directly to CEO and CTO and show what increment has team achieved in the last week, but also get steering from founders, which is super valuable. (00:19:31): Essentially founders of the company, they still review a hundred percent of screens that are being shipped and everything that you will see in the app pass this review. And there are a lot of eyeballs that were scrutinizing this and thinking of all possible edge cases and nuances that we need to consider to make sure that every single customer will be happy in this product, in this flow.
turns.zh: 关于 Revolut 的运作方式，您需要了解两件事：我们是在小型精干团队中运作，这些团队的任务是构建产品，正如我提到的，并对产品承担端到端的责任。通常他们是从零开始构建产品的人，然后他们不断发展和开发该产品。另一件事是公司非常扁平，层级也非常扁平。我们的创始人尼克和弗拉德仍然非常亲力亲为，深入了解每一款产品和业务的每一个部分的细节。每周他们都会对每个团队进行产品评审，让每个产品负责人都有机会直接向首席执行官和首席技术官展示，展示团队在上周取得的增量，同时也得到创始人的指导，这是非常有价值的。 (00:19:31)：本质上是公司的创始人，他们仍然审查 100% 正在发货的屏幕以及您将在应用程序中看到的所有内容通过此审查。有很多人在仔细审视这一点，并考虑我们需要考虑的所有可能的边缘情况和细微差别，以确保每个客户都会对这个产品、这个流程感到满意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That seems to be a consistent theme in products that are incredible is the founders are deeply involved in the experience and review everything. How many product owners are there at Revolut? Just to give people a sense by the way?
turns.zh: 这似乎是令人难以置信的产品的一致主题，因为创始人深入参与体验并审查一切。 Revolut 有多少位产品负责人？只是为了给人一种感觉吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Oh, I'm afraid to say it's already more than 150 people, maybe 170.
turns.zh: 哦，恐怕已经超过150人了，也许有170人了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. That's what I would expect. And then you said that there's kind of these three types, there's kind of like the eng type, the PM, traditional type, and there's the data product owner. When you hire the UX type of product owner today, is their previous role usually a product manager at another company?
turns.zh: 凉爽的。这就是我所期望的。然后你说有这三种类型，有工程师类型、PM、传统类型，还有数据产品所有者。当你今天雇用用户体验类型的产品负责人时，他们以前的角色通常是另一家公司的产品经理吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yes, but I would say that not necessarily it's a very experienced product manager. Well maybe even it's way more important to have this hunger for building things and having the raw intellect. And we always try to find people with these intrinsic traits rather than hiring people who are very experienced but maybe are not super excited about building things.
turns.zh: 是的，但我想说，这不一定是一位非常有经验的产品经理。好吧，也许对建造事物的渴望和拥有原始智慧更重要。我们总是试图找到具有这些内在特征的人，而不是雇用那些经验丰富但可能对构建东西不太感兴趣的人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What percentage of your product owners come from internal transfers from other functions?
turns.zh: 您的产品负责人中有多少比例来自其他职能部门的内部调动？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: It's a quite substantial part of product owners who eventually become very successful by the way. So it's like a positive self-select, so it means that someone already succeeded in another role. So it's a guaranteed culture match, it's a guaranteed domain knowledge, and then they simply grow. Usually it could be operations managers or engineers. They grow into someone who now manages the team and that's why it's a very successful path.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，这是产品所有者中相当重要的一部分，他们最终变得非常成功。所以这就像一个积极的自我选择，所以这意味着某人已经在另一个角色上取得了成功。因此，这是有保证的文化匹配，这是有保证的领域知识，然后他们就会成长。通常可以是运营经理或工程师。他们成长为现在管理团队的人，这就是为什么这是一条非常成功的道路。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So the other company on the list of top three companies that produce and hire the best PMs, according to the research I've done, Palantir. I just had someone that was at Palantir for a long time and we talked about exactly all the same questions. And interestingly so far we have kind of these three bullet points in terms of what product owners within Revolut get to do. There's a lot of ownership, there's a lot of depth and complexity, and there's a lot of focus on wow lovable products. So interestingly at Palantir also tons of ownership, also tons of depth and complexity. The other ingredient that I want to ask you about is they also have this concept of a forward deployed engineer where they put an engineer in the office of the company they're building the product from, they sit there building it for them with them. (00:22:36): And so there's a lot of skills built in terms of understanding customer problems, talking to customers, getting empathy building, things like that. Is there anything you guys do or focus on around just like talking to customers, the way you approach having your product owners work with customers, understand problems, things like that that might be helpful for people to hear?
turns.zh: 根据我所做的研究，在培养和聘用最佳产品经理的前三名公司名单上的另一家公司是 Palantir。我刚刚在 Palantir 工作了很长时间，我们讨论了完全相同的问题。有趣的是，到目前为止，我们已经掌握了 Revolut 内产品所有者要做的事情的三个要点。有很多所有权，有很多深度和复杂性，并且有很多关注令人惊叹的可爱产品。有趣的是，Palantir 还拥有大量的所有权、大量的深度和复杂性。我想问你的另一个因素是，他们也有前沿部署工程师的概念，他们在他们正在构建产品的公司的办公室里安排了一名工程师，他们坐在那里为他们构建产品。 (00:22:36)：因此，在理解客户问题、与客户交谈、建立同理心等方面需要培养很多技能。你们有没有做或关注的事情，比如与客户交谈，让产品负责人与客户合作、理解问题的方式，诸如此类的事情可能对人们听到有帮助？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: For us, it's a bit easy to reach out to customers simply because the customer base is so big, it's more than 50 million people and usually we ourselves are power users of the product. We receive our salary into Revolut and then we spend with Revolut, our friends the same. So it's like a no-brainer to talk to people continuously and even if you are not proactive in it, they will reach out. If you have a problem in the product, I guarantee that we know about it very, very soon. We've also built tools for product owners and designers to have an easy access to a panel of users via different tools so that they can just start an interviewing process or a survey or a test of different designs in a few clicks. (00:23:52): For me, it was very important to build this direct connection to customers because when you delegate such an important thing as customer research and collecting their feedback to someone, you will get a refined filtered version. You won't get these nuances of how people describe things, which emotions they feel like and so on, and where they think stuck. It's very easy to lose all those important bytes of information in this process. So I'm a strong believer that it's very important to have direct communication channel to customers.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，接触客户有点容易，因为客户群太大了，超过 5000 万人，而且通常我们自己就是产品的高级用户。我们将工资存入 Revolut，然后在 Revolut 上消费，我们的朋友也是如此。因此，不断地与人们交谈就像是理所当然的事情，即使你不主动，他们也会伸出援手。如果您的产品有问题，我保证我们很快就会知道。我们还为产品所有者和设计师构建了工具，以便通过不同的工具轻松访问用户小组，以便他们只需点击几下即可开始访谈过程或调查或不同设计的测试。 (00:23:52)：对我来说，与客户建立这种直接联系非常重要，因为当您将客户研究并收集他们的反馈这样重要的事情委托给某人时，您将获得经过精细过滤的版本。你无法理解人们如何描述事物、他们感受到哪些情绪等等以及他们认为卡在哪里的这些细微差别。在此过程中很容易丢失所有重要的信息字节。因此，我坚信与客户建立直接沟通渠道非常重要。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: As you describe this, it's funny how you guys are at the extreme opposite end of the spectrum from Palantir in terms of how easy it is for you to get feedback. They build stuff for the government and for Airbus where employees would never use a product like that or need a product like that. You guys are getting paid in Revolut using Revolut to pay for things and constantly in the product. And so I could see why there's less of a need for something like a forward deploy engineer. Okay, amazing. Let's talk about hiring then. Is there anything unique about how you approach hiring, sourcing, looking for people, what you look for in people that you think might be contributing to your alumni being so successful down the road?
turns.zh: 正如您所描述的那样，有趣的是，在获得反馈的容易程度方面，你们与 Palantir 完全相反。他们为政府和空中客车公司制造产品，而员工永远不会使用这样的产品或需要这样的产品。你们在 Revolut 中获得报酬，使用 Revolut 来支付费用，并不断在产品中获得报酬。所以我明白为什么对前沿部署工程师之类的需求较少。好吧，太棒了。那我们就来谈谈招聘的事吧。您在招聘、寻找人才、寻找人才方面有什么独特之处吗？您在寻找哪些人才，您认为这些人才可能有助于您的校友在未来取得如此成功？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I think everyone is striving for talented, skillful smart people and experienced people. Revolut values way more raw intellect and this unquenched hunger to build things rather than experience. So let me maybe bring an example. Imagine we saw this, you hire a great experienced professional with amazing regalia of achieving a lot of things, but then what I see in product, the adoption curve is usually longer than in other functions because product owners by definition are the ones who are the experts in that domain and in all those intricacies of how product is built and how it's used. So what we see from these professionals is they still take a lot of time to ramp up and sometimes they also take time to adapt to new culture or worse, they just rest on their laurels. But you already have super inflated expectations and usually their compensation is by the way, quite high and which adds up to these expectations. And I myself, after conducting maybe 400 or 500 interviews with product owners at Revolut, I also see this. (00:26:46): Unfortunately, professionals with a lot of years of experience from established companies, they don't have this strong urge to change status quo, which by the way will require toil, tears, and sweat. And that's why even if a candidate doesn't have a lot of years of experience, but they love building things, they've done it, they worked with engineers maybe by the way, maybe in their own startup or one of the best profiles that I've seen is a tech co-founder. So I think that's probably the best way to boost career is to go and found something work in a startup, build things yourself or with a very small team, work in all different areas because in startup you have to work in all different areas. And then these kind of people, they really thrive at Revolut and even if they don't have a lot of years of experience, they actually attack a specific problem. (00:28:09): They have a sense of what can cause customer pain, and they are very fast moving to solve it quickly and then that's how they get appreciation from everyone around. The team starts respecting these people because they solve some specific problem and then they take another problem, they solve it and then they take another and that's how they grow in the company.

We also allow staking crypto for example, we have on-ramp, off-ramp products, we have acquiring products. On credit, we have loans, we have a buy now per later product, we even launched mortgages. We launched first mortgages in Albania recently.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，其中一些事情本身就很重要，比如股票交易。不仅仅是股票，还有 ETF、债券，我们正在研究不同国家和加密货币的节税账户。我们还允许质押加密货币，例如，我们有入口、出口产品，我们有收购产品。在信贷方面，我们有贷款，我们有先买后买的产品，我们甚至推出了抵押贷款。我们最近在阿尔巴尼亚推出了第一批抵押贷款。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then all of these across 50 different currencies and countries.
turns.zh: 然后所有这些都跨越 50 种不同的货币和国家。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, 50 different jurisdictions each with its own regulation, with its own requirements.
turns.zh: 是的，50 个不同的司法管辖区都有自己的法规和要求。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, boy. It's a good example of Paul Graham has this concept of schlep blindness or schlepping where people want to avoid hard problems, but that's where the big opportunities are, solving really gnarly, painful problems. And that's basically what you guys did.
turns.zh: 哦，男孩。这是保罗·格雷厄姆（Paul Graham）的一个很好的例子，他提出了“拖沓盲目”或“拖拖拉拉”的概念，人们想要避免困难的问题，但这就是巨大的机会所在，解决真正棘手的、痛苦的问题。这基本上就是你们所做的。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, that's one of the things that excites me maybe the most at Revolut. The market is so big and there are still a lot of very inefficient players, and as a result, customers have a lot of problems that are unsolved. While we grow insanely and I think will soon be... When I joined, we had maybe just slightly north to 20 million customers. Now we are 50 million customers. Soon we'll be at 100 million customers. The degree of surrounding each customer with the ecosystem of our products extends a lot. So they become more and more people start using Revolut as their main bank account. They start receiving their salary into Revolut, holding their savings into Revolut because they love the product more. And so we can easily do another, I don't know, 2, 3X, 4X in customer base growth, but we can also do another 10X growth in how actively these people are using the product. So it's let's say what, 30, 40X to current, 45 billion valuation. Right? So it's a like a trillion-dollar company easily.
turns.zh: 是的，这可能是 Revolut 最令我兴奋的事情之一。市场这么大，仍然存在很多效率很低的参与者，导致客户有很多问题没有解决。虽然我们疯狂地成长，而且我认为很快就会……当我加入时，我们的客户数量可能略高于 2000 万。现在我们有 5000 万客户。很快我们的客户数量将达到 1 亿。我们产品的生态系统包围每个客户的程度大大扩展。因此，越来越多的人开始使用 Revolut 作为他们的主要银行账户。他们开始将工资存入 Revolut，并将积蓄存入 Revolut，因为他们更喜欢该产品。因此，我们可以轻松地实现另一个（我不知道）客户群增长 2 倍、3 倍、4 倍，但我们也可以使这些人使用该产品的积极性再增长 10 倍。那么，我们可以说，目前 450 亿美元估值的 30 倍、40 倍。正确的？所以它很容易成为一家万亿美元的公司。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And on that note, I mean what I'm hearing is it's still a good time to join. There's a massive upside. So I know you guys are hiring, we'll just note that real quick. You're hiring product owners and a bunch of other roles, I imagine?
turns.zh: 就这一点而言，我的意思是我听到的是现在仍然是加入的好时机。有巨大的上升空间。所以我知道你们正在招聘，我们会很快注意到这一点。我想你们正在招聘产品负责人和许多其他角色？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, yeah. Well, as someone who owns the product function, I'm especially interested in product owners obviously, but we hire a lot of roles. I think we have maybe 3 or 400 open positions currently.
turns.zh: 是啊是啊。嗯，作为负责产品功能的人，我显然对产品负责人特别感兴趣，但我们雇佣了很多角色。我认为我们目前可能有 3 或 400 个空缺职位。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh my God. Okay. I want to talk a bit about new stuff that you work on. So new products that you decide to invest in. Is there anything that you've figured out about just how to set up new products for success? Because a lot of the stuff we've been talking about is staying on top of stuff that you're iterating on and making better. What have you learned about just helping new products succeed?
turns.zh: 我的天啊。好的。我想谈谈你正在做的新事情。您决定投资的新产品。关于如何建立新产品以获得成功，您有什么想法吗？因为我们一直在谈论的很多东西都是在你正在迭代和改进的东西之上。关于帮助新产品取得成功，您学到了什么？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, so we launched quite a few products that you actually maybe wouldn't expect from a bank starting with crypto that was insanely successful, but also non-financial services like booking a hotel through Revolut app, our loyalty program, rev points, which is sort of disrupting European market where people don't get great benefits from spending with card. In the US you can easily get, like what? 2% cashback with a credit card or in some sort of point. In Europe they don't have it. And we are actually the first to build a program on card spend rewarding people with really meaningful or monetary rewards. In the manner that I described. We understood, okay, what's the recipe of this success to then scale it and reproduce? So we built a new bets framework and essentially everyone can come up with a new idea. It could be a product owner, but it could be anyone, and they need to show some key important things which you usually can expect from a startup like market is there, business case is there. (00:46:15): We know that we can do it way better than competitors leverage and for example, some things that we have obviously some concepts of product and then what customer problem we're solving and so on. And there is very little bureaucracy, again, thanks to having founder hands-on, we can easily get a green light on anything, start launching it quickly. What we do is assemble same lean team with just a few people to build first version and then iterate and iterate. And the main thing here is to build first version very quickly to get feedback, but then not scale it before you polish the product. But then after we make sure that all metrics are fine, retention is great, we start scaling it. And the good news is that it can be instantly multiplied by our 50 million customer base and get great traction. So for example, one of the products that you mentioned, joint accounts essentially an account that you could have with a significant other one was one of the recently launched feature and it grew significantly and now it has over a million active users.
turns.zh: 是的，所以我们推出了相当多的产品，你实际上可能不会想到银行会从加密货币开始，取得了巨大的成功，但也推出了非金融服务，例如通过 Revolut 应用程序预订酒店、我们的忠诚度计划、转速积分，这在某种程度上扰乱了欧洲市场，在欧洲市场，人们无法从用卡消费中获得巨大好处。在美国你很容易就能得到，比如什么？使用信用卡或某种积分可获得 2% 的现金返还。在欧洲他们没有。事实上，我们是第一个制定卡消费计划的公司，为人们提供真正有意义的奖励或金钱奖励。按照我描述的方式。我们明白了，好吧，这种成功的秘诀是什么，然后才能扩大规模并复制？因此，我们建立了一个新的投注框架，基本上每个人都可以想出新的想法。它可以是产品负责人，但也可以是任何人，他们需要展示一些你通常可以从初创公司那里得到的关键重要信息，比如市场在那里，商业案例在那里。 (00:46:15)：我们知道我们可以比竞争对手做得更好，例如，我们显然有一些产品概念，然后我们正在解决哪些客户问题等等。而且官僚主义也很少，再次感谢创始人的亲力亲为，我们可以轻松地批准任何事情，并快速开始启动它。我们所做的就是用几个人组建同样的精益团队来构建第一个版本，然后迭代再迭代。这里最重要的是非常快速地构建第一个版本以获得反馈，但在完善产品之前不要扩展它。但在我们确保所有指标都很好、保留率很高之后，我们开始扩展它。好消息是，它可以立即乘以我们的 5000 万客户群，并获得巨大的吸引力。例如，您提到的产品之一，联合帐户本质上是您可以与另一个重要帐户一起拥有的帐户，是最近推出的功能之一，并且它增长显着，现在拥有超过一百万的活跃用户。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I hear one of the ways you kind of approach these early products differently is you guys invest a lot in actually making it good and not just like a scrappy MVP. Does that ring a bell? Does that resonate?
turns.zh: 我听说你们以不同的方式处理这些早期产品的方式之一是，你们投入了大量资金来真正使其变得更好，而不仅仅是像一个斗志旺盛的 MVP。这是否敲响了警钟？这引起共鸣吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Indeed, that's what I may be meant by keeping your first version narrowed down to a small user base. But even in this case, we still make sure that the product is well. So no one is excluded from this requirement of building a super polished product. It takes time, but it pays off. The thing is that when you launch a scrappy version and it's not getting traction, how do you know? Is it because the underlying idea is wrong or maybe your product just sucks and you need to improve it? So by forcing everyone to build a product that people will love by building a wow product, we kind of cut out this part of uncertainty. So bottom line, we can cut down the product in terms of functionality to just most critical features, but we will never compromise on the quality and UX and the aesthetics.
turns.zh: 事实上，这就是我将第一个版本缩小到较小的用户群的意思。但即使在这种情况下，我们仍然确保产品是好的。因此，没有人被排除在构建超级抛光产品的这一要求之外。这需要时间，但会有回报。问题是，当你推出一个杂乱的版本但它没有受到关注时，你怎么知道呢？是因为潜在的想法是错误的，还是因为你的产品很糟糕，你需要改进它？因此，通过强迫每个人通过打造令人惊叹的产品来打造人们会喜欢的产品，我们就消除了这部分不确定性。因此，最重要的是，我们可以将产品的功能削减为最关键的功能，但我们永远不会在质量、用户体验和美观上妥协。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: An interesting advantage you guys have that I'm realizing as you talk is most of the stuff you launch is stuff that is clearly something people will want because it's stuff that they get other places, but they get the advantages of it being integrated into all the other features and products you have. So it's like a cryptocurrency product. It's kind of like, okay, yeah, people would love a great cryptocurrency product built into this or joint accounts. So there's almost like a benefit of just like, okay, the people will want this, now let's just make it work really well with everything else we got and not hurt. You almost don't need to be the best at every product, although it sounds like you still try to be the best.
turns.zh: 你们有一个有趣的优势，我在你们讲话时意识到，你们推出的大部分产品显然都是人们想要的东西，因为这些东西是他们从其他地方获得的，但他们得到了将其集成到你们拥有的所有其他功能和产品中的优势。所以它就像一个加密货币产品。这有点像，好吧，是的，人们会喜欢这个或联合账户中内置的出色的加密货币产品。所以这几乎是一个好处，好吧，人们会想要这个，现在让我们让它与我们拥有的其他一切很好地配合，而不受到伤害。你几乎不需要在每件产品上都做到最好，尽管听起来你仍然试图成为最好的。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: But we must be the best. Yeah, a hundred percent.
turns.zh: 但我们必须是最好的。是的，百分之一百。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: But there's also, if you don't have the best joint account, but all the other stuff is awesome, people are like, "All right, it's fine. It just makes my life easier." But tell me what I might be missing because-
turns.zh: 但也有，如果你没有最好的联名账户，但所有其他东西都很棒，人们会说，“好吧，没关系。它只是让我的生活更轻松。”但请告诉我我可能会错过什么，因为-

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: So I think there are those kind of table stakes that we're building that anyone would expect from a bank. For example, savings account, right? It's just a basic thing that if a bank is not providing savings account, you wouldn't even consider it. But then we make sure that our rates are very competitive, if not the best. Then we make sure that there is no bad UX. Some banks, for example, they don't allow you to withdraw instantly and there are delays or they don't pay interest on daily basis. We will never do that. We will allow you if you want to move money out, you will be able to do it. You won't lose any interest. And interest is being paid daily and this is a fully flexible product. And then on top of it, what I would call maybe some delighters is we will allow you to open the savings account in many currencies. (00:50:49): So we want to add different currencies because now interest rates are going down, so people might find it valuable to open a savings account in, for example, I know in Europe, Swedish Krona interest rates are higher than Europe, but it could be even something like Brazilian Real with 12% interest rate versus 2 or 3% on euros. And then as the cherry on top, there is this all that in an amazing, you have very smooth, you can set custom wallpapers, you can set goals, you can automate a spare change towards your savings and all those features. So there is an underlying basic fundamental layer that where you need to be just on par with competition, but then there are a lot of things on top that just make people love your product way more. And obviously there are a lot of synergies in between those things. So yeah, thinking of crypto, you can just receive crypto on your wallet and then you can just instantly convert it to cash on your account or just spend it with your card. How amazing can it be? Just buy a coffee with Ethereum.
turns.zh: 所以我认为我们正在建立的赌注是任何人都期望从银行获得的。例如，储蓄账户，对吧？这是一个基本的事情，如果银行不提供储蓄账户，你甚至不会考虑它。但我们会确保我们的价格即使不是最好的，也是非常有竞争力的。然后我们确保没有糟糕的用户体验。例如，有些银行不允许您立即取款，并且存在延迟或不按日支付利息。我们永远不会那样做。如果您想将资金转出，我们将允许您这样做。你不会失去任何兴趣。利息每天支付，这是一个完全灵活的产品。最重要的是，我所说的也许是一些令人高兴的事情是我们将允许您以多种货币开设储蓄账户。 (00:50:49)：所以我们想添加不同的货币，因为现在利率正在下降，所以人们可能会发现在欧洲开设储蓄账户很有价值，例如，我知道在欧洲，瑞典克朗的利率高于欧洲，但甚至可能是像巴西雷亚尔这样的货币，利率为 12%，而欧元的利率为 2% 或 3%。然后，作为顶部的樱桃，这一切都令人惊叹，您拥有非常流畅的功能，您可以设置自定义壁纸，您可以设定目标，您可以自动对您的储蓄进行备用更改以及所有这些功能。因此，有一个基本的基本层，您需要在其中与竞争对手保持同等水平，但除此之外还有很多东西可以让人们更喜欢您的产品。显然，这些事情之间存在很多协同作用。所以，是的，考虑到加密货币，您可以在钱包上接收加密货币，然后您可以立即将其转换为您帐户上的现金，或者直接用您的卡消费。能有多神奇呢？只需用以太坊买一杯咖啡即可。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. Okay, let me take this opportunity to try to summarize what I've learned from you so far in terms of what you guys have figured out about creating incredible product leaders. They go on to do wonderful things and basically one of the top three most successful companies at this. So there's kind of these two buckets as I talked to you and the Palantir guy, there's kind of like the hiring piece and then there's what you do to help incubate this kind of forge for incredible product leaders. So in what you do internally, kind of the four bullet points I've got here is give people a lot of ownership. They're essentially GMs of the product, the feature. (00:52:46): There's a lot of focus on depth and complexity and getting really good at solving really gnarly problems. And then there's a focus on building wow products, amazing lovable products that have a very high bar. And then there's kind of a subtle point that I think is probably impactful here is just working closely with detail-obsessed founders or product leaders like you and learning from you all and just seeing the value and impact of being super detail oriented. On that bucket, is there anything else that you think is super core that I missed before we get to hiring?
turns.zh: 我喜欢那个。好吧，让我借此机会尝试总结一下到目前为止我从你们那里学到的东西，即你们在创造令人难以置信的产品领导者方面的想法。他们继续做一些很棒的事情，基本上是这方面最成功的三大公司之一。因此，当我与您和 Palantir 人员交谈时，有这两个方面的内容，就像招聘部分一样，然后您会采取哪些措施来帮助培育这种令人难以置信的产品领导者。因此，在您内部所做的事情中，我在这里提出的四个要点是给予人们很大的所有权。他们本质上是产品、功能的总经理。 (00:52:46)：人们非常关注深度和复杂性，并真正擅长解决真正棘手的问题。然后重点是打造令人惊叹的产品，令人惊叹的可爱产品，具有很高的标准。然后有一个微妙的点，我认为这里可能有影响力，就是与像你这样注重细节的创始人或产品领导者密切合作，向你们所有人学习，并看到超级细节导向的价值和影响。在这个方面，还有什么是你认为在我们开始招聘之前我错过的超级核心吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, I would just maybe highlight the aspect of this going deep into details. There are two main streams. First is let's say being technical, understanding how underlying systems work, but second is also building empathy towards customers. Understand the possible contexts and making sure that your product will satisfy each one of them.
turns.zh: 是的，我可能只是想强调一下深入细节的方面。有两个主流。首先是技术性的，了解底层系统是如何工作的，其次是建立对客户的同理心。了解可能的情况并确保您的产品能够满足每一种情况。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's a great point. So it's actually understanding the bare metal of what is happening and how it's possible, and then making the experience as simple and wowable as possible.
turns.zh: 这是一个很好的观点。因此，它实际上是了解正在发生的事情及其可能性，然后使体验尽可能简单和令人惊叹。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: There is also a third aspect, but it's a boring one and it's complying with all possible regulations and making sure that your product will satisfy the regulator, but it's also an important part of the job.
turns.zh: 还有第三个方面，但这是一个无聊的方面，它遵守所有可能的法规并确保你的产品能够满足监管机构的要求，但这也是工作的重要组成部分。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What I get from that is just building patience with all-
turns.zh: 我从中得到的只是对所有人建立耐心-

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I would say it's actually being able to unblock your team and that sometimes require product owners to steam roll changes because it also means that you could easily get stuck with a lot of people just looking into each other and thinking, "Okay, can they approve it? Can they not approve it?" We try to innovate on it. We try to automate as many things as possible. We use even AI models for that, but it also requires a product owner to be able to get things done, just getting people down to consensus and understanding how your stakeholders, how to get them to the necessary decision and then blocking UTM so that eventually the value is shipped to customers.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，它实际上能够解锁你的团队，有时需要产品负责人推动变更，因为这也意味着你很容易陷入与很多人互相审视并思考“好吧，他们可以批准它吗？他们可以不批准它吗？”我们尝试在此基础上进行创新。我们尝试使尽可能多的事情实现自动化。为此，我们甚至使用人工智能模型，但它还要求产品所有者能够完成工作，只需让人们达成共识并了解利益相关者如何，如何让他们做出必要的决定，然后阻止 UTM，以便最终将价值传递给客户。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. So essentially it's just getting done, plowing through blockers, dealing with many stakeholders.
turns.zh: 惊人的。所以本质上，它只是完成任务，克服障碍，与许多利益相关者打交道。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah. That's always the most important.
turns.zh: 是的。这始终是最重要的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. That's a great addition. I could see why that would be really helpful for folks that are trying to get ahead in their career. And then on the hiring piece, what you look for is raw intellect, drive hunger, passion essentially. Those are the first two. And then interestingly, non-senior, not people with a ton of experience in the problem space, more so focusing on intellect and hunger. Is there anything else in that bucket that you think is important that leads to people being really successful?
turns.zh: 好的。这是一个很好的补充。我明白为什么这对于那些试图在职业生涯中取得成功的人来说非常有帮助。然后在招聘方面，你寻找的是原始智慧、驱动饥饿感和激情。这是前两个。有趣的是，非资深人士，不是在问题领域拥有丰富经验的人，更关注智力和饥饿。您认为在这个桶中还有其他什么重要的东西可以让人们真正成功吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Most importantly, it's again, getting things done, getting your hands dirty, and great product owners are very hands-on. They don't think of themselves as managers who just give tasks to people and wait them to complete it. They just go and get things done and they understand that most important things they will likely have to do themselves, and they understand that there needs to be relentless focus on execution, and if something is 99% done, it's closer to 0% rather than 100%.
turns.zh: 最重要的是，再次强调，把事情做好，亲自动手，优秀的产品负责人都非常亲力亲为。他们并不认为自己是管理者，只是将任务分配给人们并等待他们完成。他们只是去把事情做好，他们明白最重要的事情可能需要他们自己做，他们明白需要不懈地关注执行，如果某件事完成了 99%，那么它更接近 0%，而不是 100%。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Whoa, say more there. Is the kind of insight there is just things seem like they're 99% done, but they're actually very far from being done?
turns.zh: 呵呵，那你就多说点吧。是否有一种洞察力，就是事情看起来已经完成了 99%，但实际上距离完成还很远？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Sometimes the product is built, but then product owners are the ones who also make sure that, for example, customer care team or sales and marketing team are using it to a full extent because without it, it could be just another useless feature, and no one knows about it.
turns.zh: 有时产品是构建出来的，但产品负责人还要确保客户服务团队或销售和营销团队充分利用它，因为如果没有它，它可能只是另一个无用的功能，而且没有人知道它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is super cool. I like that mentality. Let me ask you something completely different. What's kind of the story of you landing at Revolut? I know you had to move your family. It was a whole adventure.
turns.zh: 那太酷了。我喜欢这种心态。让我问你一些完全不同的问题。你来到 Revolut 的故事是怎样的？我知道你必须搬家。这是一次完整的冒险。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: My journey into Revolut actually coincided with me moving to the UK, so it was a completely new environment for myself. It's a huge stress load for the brain as well. And it's not only about using the other side of the lane on the road in the UK, but also it's a lot of things, for example, in the industry, some concepts that I've never heard about, and actually I've never worked at FinTech before, so I also changed the industry. So it was a complete turnaround for me and for my career, but I was very determined and excited about it because everyone who I've been talking to, they were saying Revolut is like it's top talent is at Revolut, all best product people are at Revolut, and I really wanted to be part of this great team. (00:58:11): Eventually it actually appeared to be advantageous for me because I also had this fresh view on things and even in the Revolut app, which is actually way, way better than other banks products. But even there I found some things that for me, because of this lack of context, they were not intuitive and I worked hard with the team to change that.
turns.zh: 我进入 Revolut 的旅程实际上与我搬到英国同时发生，所以这对我来说是一个全新的环境。这对大脑来说也是一个巨大的压力负荷。而且不仅仅是在英国马路上使用车道的另一边，还有很多东西，比如在行业里，一些我从来没有听说过的概念，而且其实我以前从来没有在FinTech工作过，所以我也改变了这个行业。所以这对我和我的职业生涯来说都是一次彻底的转变，但我对此非常坚定和兴奋，因为与我交谈过的每个人都说 Revolut 就像顶尖人才都在 Revolut，所有最好的产品人员都在 Revolut，我真的很想成为这个伟大团队的一员。 (00:58:11)：最终它实际上对我来说似乎是有利的，因为我对事物甚至在 Revolut 应用程序中也有这种新的看法，这实际上比其他银行产品要好得多。但即使在那里，我也发现了一些对我来说由于缺乏背景而变得不直观的事情，我与团队一起努力改变这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, great. I'm going to take us to recurring segment of the podcast. I'm going to take us to Fail Corner. So in Fail Corner, the idea here is people come on this podcast, they share all these stories of success, everything's always going great, but in reality, things don't often go great, and there's a lot of things that don't go right. Is there a story you could share where things went wrong in your career, where you failed with a product you were building or a moment in your career where things were looking really bad?
turns.zh: 好的，太好了。我将带我们进入播客的重复部分。我要带我们去失败角。所以在《失败角》中，这里的想法是人们来到这个播客，他们分享所有这些成功的故事，一切总是进展顺利，但实际上，事情并不经常进展顺利，而且有很多事情进展不顺利。您是否可以分享一个故事：您的职业生涯中出现了问题，您正在开发的产品失败了，或者您职业生涯中的某个时刻看起来非常糟糕？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I think the most spectacular failures is probably were on the earliest stage of my career, which I studied back at university and maybe in my second year of university I started building some things, different startups, and one of them was actually a product that makes me proud even now because it was like what, 15 years ago? So 2010, meaning still no one really had even iPhones back then and me and my friends, we started building a website that allows people to buy tickets to the cinema so that they can skip the line so they don't need to come in advance to select best seats and they can just buy a ticket online and go to the seats directly. Something that today seems as a commodity. Back then no one had it. (01:00:15): People were using pieces of paper and we built an end-to-end system because not only we needed to build a website, but we also needed to build hardware to scan those tickets, for example. And to have these tickets in digital format, we needed to hack SMS standard because again, people didn't have smartphones. They had these Nokias and we were sending images, QR codes inside an SMS, which is like a hack of the standards in a way. And then we were scanning those things with our own devices and we built our own devices with scanners, and we actually created these beautiful devices made from stainless steel, which looked really nice inside the cinema halls. (01:01:12): And I remember how I was excited about it with my friends. We were like, "What an amazing thing." It's like, look, we are bringing future here, but we actually spent all our investment on this hardware and we were expecting that everyone will just rush into using our system. But it was a very low share of customers who started buying tickets online because people were not ready for it, which was growing quite slowly. And eventually we had to close it because we simply ran out of money because we spent all of it on this hardware without any proven business model. So something that currently looks like an obvious mistake back then, we were just enjoying building a product that we would love to use ourselves, which I think is the right principle, but it also was a very painful lesson. You need to stay lean, you need to validate things before you scale them. You need to think way more about the run rate of your business. So there were a lot of painful lessons for me. Since then, I also try to avoid working with hardware.
turns.zh: 我认为最引人注目的失败可能是在我职业生涯的最早阶段，我在大学学习了这一点，也许在大学第二年我开始建造一些东西，不同的初创公司，其中一个实际上是一个让我现在感到自豪的产品，因为它就像 15 年前一样？所以到了2010年，当时还没有人真正拥有iPhone，而我和我的朋友们，我们开始建立一个网站，允许人们购买电影院的门票，这样他们就可以跳过排队，这样他们就不需要提前来选择最好的座位，他们可以直接在网上买票然后直接去座位。今天看来是一种商品。那时没有人拥有它。 (01:00:15)：人们使用纸张，我们构建了一个端到端系统，因为我们不仅需要构建一个网站，而且还需要构建硬件来扫描这些票证等。为了获得这些数字格式的门票，我们需要破解短信标准，因为人们没有智能手机。他们有这些诺基亚，而我们在短信中发送图像、二维码，这在某种程度上就像是对标准的黑客攻击。然后我们用我们自己的设备扫描这些东西，我们用扫描仪构建了我们自己的设备，我们实际上创建了这些由不锈钢制成的漂亮设备，它们在电影院大厅内看起来非常漂亮。 (01:01:12)：我记得我和朋友们对此感到多么兴奋。我们当时想，“多么了不起的事情啊。”就像，看，我们在这里带来了未来，但我们实际上把所有投资都花在了这个硬件上，我们期望每个人都会急于使用我们的系统。但开始在线购买门票的客户比例非常低，因为人们还没有做好准备，而且增长速度相当缓慢。最终我们不得不关闭它，因为我们根本没钱了，因为我们把所有的钱都花在了这个没有任何经过验证的商业模式的硬件上。因此，现在看来这是一个明显的错误，我们只是享受构建一个我们自己喜欢使用的产品，我认为这是正确的原则，但这也是一个非常痛苦的教训。您需要保持精益，需要在扩展之前对其进行验证。您需要更多地考虑业务的运行率。所以给我带来了很多惨痛的教训。从那时起，我也尽量避免与硬件打交道。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I was just going to say that's a common challenge for startups trying to get right into hardware, although I wouldn't be surprised now if Revolut launches something another product, and this is a new product line of Revolut now that you've had that experience.
turns.zh: 我只是想说，对于试图进入硬件领域的初创公司来说，这是一个常见的挑战，尽管如果 Revolut 现在推出其他产品，我不会感到惊讶，而且这是 Revolut 的新产品线，既然您已经有了这种经验。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: We launched a POS terminals required.
turns.zh: 我们推出了所需的POS终端。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: All right, there we go. Dmitry, before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that we haven't touched on that you think might be really helpful for listeners to hear? Maybe a last wisdom nugget that you haven't already shared, or even just something to kind of double down on that you've already shared?
turns.zh: 好吧，我们开始吧。德米特里（Dmitry），在我们开始非常激动人心的闪电回合之前，还有什么我们没有提到但您认为可能对听众真正有帮助的内容吗？也许是您尚未分享的最后一个智慧金块，或者甚至只是您已经分享过的东西的加倍？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: No, I think that it was an amazing chat and thanks, Lenny. We covered a lot of different topics. I would just maybe summarize that if you're excited to build certain things, never hesitate to do it. The best way to do it is probably your own startup, and it also what will give you the steepest possible learning curve, but then if you want to join a company, try to choose the one that has the highest entrepreneurial spirit and that will allow you to work as closer to a mode of a founder as you possibly can.
turns.zh: 不，我认为这是一次很棒的聊天，谢谢，莱尼。我们讨论了很多不同的主题。我可能会总结一下，如果您对构建某些东西感到兴奋，请毫不犹豫地去做。最好的方法可能是你自己创业，它也会给你尽可能陡峭的学习曲线，但如果你想加入一家公司，请尝试选择一家具有最高创业精神的公司，这将使你尽可能接近创始人的模式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's a recurring theme in these conversations I'm having with companies that produce the PMs that have the steepest career trajectory. And so that advice is exactly what I'm taking away from this too, assuming you want your career to accelerate really quickly after you go work at this company. Okay, Dmitry, with that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 这是我与那些培养出具有最陡峭职业轨迹的产品经理的公司进行的对话中反复出现的主题。因此，假设您希望在这家公司工作后您的职业生涯能够迅速加速，那么这个建议也正是我从中得到的建议。好的，德米特里，我们已经进入了非常激动人心的闪电回合。你准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yes. Let's go.
turns.zh: 是的。我们走吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Here we go. Okay. First question, what are two or three books that you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 开始了。好的。第一个问题，您向其他人推荐最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: The Hard Thing About Hard Things by Ben Horowitz. Actually read it quite some time ago, but I found myself recommending it to other product managers most often. It's actually illustrative that to be a great product manager, someone needs to strive to being a great CEO. And besides this book emphasizes the importance of building systematic solutions and scalable solutions, which is critical for scaling a company. Also being honest on how important it is to grind stuff. And then second book is, I read it more recently, Build by Tony Fadell. I was really inspired by this one, especially given how I appreciate how it's not easy to build hardware and what Tony was describing there is just super exciting and inspiring. And also I think that there are different archetypes of product managers. There are people who tend to disrupt things more. Personally I think about myself as a builder, so Tony's principles that he highlighted in the book that they resonate with me a lot.
turns.zh: 本·霍洛维茨 (Ben Horowitz) 的《困难中的困难》。实际上很久以前就读过它，但我发现自己最常向其他产品经理推荐它。这实际上说明了，要成为一名出色的产品经理，就需要努力成为一名出色的首席执行官。除此之外，本书还强调了构建系统解决方案和可扩展解决方案的重要性，这对于扩展公司规模至关重要。还要诚实地了解研磨东西的重要性。第二本书是我最近读过的，托尼·法德尔（Tony Fadell）写的《Build》。我真的受到了这个启发，特别是考虑到我非常欣赏构建硬件是多么不容易，而托尼在那里描述的内容非常令人兴奋和鼓舞人心。而且我认为产品经理有不同的原型。有些人更倾向于破坏事情。就我个人而言，我认为自己是一名建设者，因此托尼在书中强调的原则与我产生了很大的共鸣。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm trying to get Tony on the podcast. If anyone listening knows Tony Fadell and can nudge him, "Hey, say yes to Lenny," that'd be great. I've been in touch with his team, but he's not doing podcasts right now, but I'm trying to get him on. Okay, moving on. Do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show that you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 我正在努力让托尼加入播客。如果听众中有人认识托尼·法德尔（Tony Fadell）并且可以轻推他，“嘿，对莱尼说是”，那就太好了。我一直在与他的团队保持联系，但他现在没有做播客，但我正在努力让他加入。好的，继续。您最近有最喜欢的电影或电视节目吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I think the last movie I watched was Oppenheimer and I really liked it. I always love watching biopics. I think they give kind of a perspective and let you think about things in perspective.
turns.zh: 我想我看的最后一部电影是《奥本海默》，我真的很喜欢它。我一直喜欢看传记片。我认为它们提供了一种视角，让你能够正确地思考事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a favorite product you recently discovered that you really love?
turns.zh: 您最近发现有一款您真正喜欢的最喜欢的产品吗？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Manus is a great thing.
turns.zh: 马努斯是一件伟大的事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The AI agent?
turns.zh: 人工智能代理？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. It's just like I was super impressed how... I was mesmerized. It's so autonomous and smooth, and I just spent a few hours vibe coding and I created this JavaScript app that sends me a rare English word every day to learn and remember, and it worked, and I was just amazed.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。就好像我印象非常深刻……我被迷住了。它是如此自主和流畅，我只花了几个小时进行 vivi 编码，并创建了这个 JavaScript 应用程序，它每天都会向我发送一个罕见的英语单词来学习和记住，它起作用了，我感到很惊讶。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What's a word you learned?
turns.zh: 你学到了什么单词？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Ineffable. It was the yesterday's word.
turns.zh: 不可言喻。这是昨天的话。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. It's still going. That's great. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to, you find useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 我喜欢那个。它还在继续。那太棒了。您是否有一条最喜欢的、经常回顾的人生格言，您发现它在工作或生活中很有用？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I love this phrase. I think Eisenhower said it, "Plans are worthless, but planning is everything." It's like we often say how important it is to be flexible and agile and adjust to change in circumstances, but it doesn't allow us to actually not have a plan at all. It's important for us to remember that we always need to think many steps ahead and while being flexible, we also need to think things thoroughly.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这句话。我认为艾森豪威尔说过，“计划毫无价值，但计划就是一切。”就像我们经常说灵活敏捷并根据环境变化进行调整是多么重要，但这并不意味着我们实际上根本没有计划。对我们来说，重要的是要记住，我们总是需要提前考虑很多步骤，在保持灵活性的同时，我们还需要彻底思考事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Final question. For folks that are maybe checking out Revolut for the first time that want to play with it or already users. What's the most underrated feature? What's something that you think people should check out maybe they're not aware of, or even just like a UX, I don't know, animation, something fun that people may not know about?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题。对于那些可能是第一次查看 Revolut、想要使用它或已经是用户的人。最被低估的功能是什么？您认为人们应该检查哪些可能他们不知道的东西，或者甚至只是像用户体验，我不知道，动画，人们可能不知道的有趣的东西？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: The thing that is not yet widely used, but I really loved it, is what we call a wealth protection. So if you go to settings, you can enable a limit for any transfers outside of Revolut. If you want to do a transfer above this limit, you'll have to do a selfie check, which is our proprietary technology. We do a video selfie here. It allows us to make sure that it's you, no one else is doing the transfer, and it's actually almost as smooth as face ID and the way the team built it is really great. I'm really proud of those guys.
turns.zh: 尚未广泛使用但我真的很喜欢它的东西就是我们所说的财富保护。因此，如果您进入设置，您可以为 Revolut 之外的任何转账启用限制。如果您想进行超过此限制的转账，则必须进行自拍检查，这是我们的专有技术。我们在这里拍了一段自拍视频。它使我们能够确保是您本人在进行传输，没有其他人在进行传输，而且它实际上几乎与面容 ID 一样顺利，而且团队构建它的方式非常出色。我真的为这些人感到骄傲。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Dmitry, you guys are doing something very special. I really appreciate you spending so much time with me chatting through all the things you guys have figured out. I think this is going to help a lot of different companies level up the way they think about product and for people to join Revolut that want to experience this and accelerate their career. So thank you for being here. Two final questions. Where can folks find you if they want to reach out and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 德米特里，你们正在做一些非常特别的事情。我真的很感谢你们花这么多时间和我一起讨论你们已经弄清楚的所有事情。我认为这将帮助许多不同的公司提升他们对产品的思考方式，并帮助人们加入 Revolut 来体验这一点并加速他们的职业生涯。谢谢你来到这里。最后两个问题。如果人们想要联系您，可以在哪里找到您？听众如何对您有用？

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: I think the best way is to find me on LinkedIn and yeah, I would be happy to receive a note from anyone on how we can improve the product and any feedback on the product. And also if you know someone who can be a great fit to Revolut after you've listened to what I've told, then yeah, I would be grateful for that as well.
turns.zh: 我认为最好的方法是在 LinkedIn 上找到我，是的，我很高兴收到任何人关于我们如何改进产品的说明以及有关产品的任何反馈。而且，如果您在听完我的介绍后认识一个非常适合 Revolut 的人，那么是的，我也会对此表示感激。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. You're about to get a flood of applications. Get prepared. Dmitry, thank you.
turns.zh: 惊人的。您将收到大量申请。做好准备。德米特里，谢谢你。

turns.speaker: Dmitry Zlokazov
turns.en: Yeah, Lenny, thanks a lot. It was amazing time. Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 是的，莱尼，非常感谢。那是一段美妙的时光。非常感谢。

turns.zh: 相同的。再见大家。 (01:09:38)：非常感谢您的收听。如果您发现这很有价值，您可以在 Apple Podcasts、Spotify 或您最喜欢的播客应用程序上订阅该节目。另外，请考虑给我们评分或留下评论，因为这确实有助于其他听众找到播客。您可以在 lennyspodcast.com 上找到所有过去的剧集或了解有关该节目的更多信息。下一集见。
